LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 6.3.1 COMPARISON OF ADVERBS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.3: Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Comparison of Adverbs

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Comparison of Adverbs. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How do we compare things?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the degrees of comparison in adverbs
2. use positive, comparative and superlative degrees of adverbs in sentences

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify the degrees of comparison in adverbs
   In simple words: practise until you can identify the degrees of comparison in adverbs. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. use positive, comparative and superlative degrees of adverbs in sentences
   In simple words: practise until you can use positive, comparative and superlative degrees of adverbs in sentences. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Comparison of Adverbs using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Comparison of Adverbs in the examples.
2. Explain Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Comparison of Adverbs to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Comparison of Adverbs.
4. Show that you can: identify the degrees of comparison in adverbs

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Comparison of Adverbs using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Comparison of Adverbs important for a Grade 9 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Practise using different degrees of adverbs in sentences,
2. Listen to an audio clip or read a passage featuring the comparison of adverbs,
3. Discuss the rules for comparison of adverbs,
4. Use various degrees of adverbs during a role play,
5. Digital literacy: It is promoted as the learner listens to an audio clip on the comparison of adverbs.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we compare things?
2. Which words are used to make comparison?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify the degrees of comparison in adverbs
2. use positive, comparative and superlative degrees of adverbs in sentences

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
